title: FastTree: Optimizing Attention Computation for Tree-Structured LLM Inference
problem: LLM serving systems that share KV cache via radix trees (prefix sharing) waste compute by running separate GEMV attention for each query even when many queries share a large common KV prefix, failing to exploit the tree structure for hardware-efficient GEMM.
motivation: GEMV (single query against KV cache) has poor tensor core utilization; when multiple queries share a prefix, grouping their attention into GEMM would dramatically improve hardware efficiency, but existing kernels do not exploit the tree topology.
method: The algorithm uses a greedy approach to partition the KV-cache radix tree (a tree structure representing shared prefixes in the cache) into two groups: shared context and query-specific parts. A specialized attention kernel based on FlashAttention processes the shared context once and reuses it across all queries in a group by processing them together. This transforms slow individual matrix-vector operations (GEMV) into a single fast batched matrix-matrix operation (GEMM) that hardware can efficiently execute.
key_novelty: The algorithm greedily assigns edges in the KV-cache tree to identify query groups that can share computation, converting slow per-query matrix-vector operations into fast batched matrix-matrix operations.
contributions: Binary edge assignment algorithm for grouping radix-tree nodes into context-query groups for query aggregation
FlashAttention-style tiled kernel with shared KV reuse across aggregated queries (GEMV-to-GEMM)
2.2x throughput improvement over SGLang+FlashInfer on tree-structured serving workloads
Kernel-level: 5.1x over FlashAttention, 4.2x over FlashInfer, 10.6x over DeFT

metrics.speedup: 2.2x system throughput over SGLang+FlashInfer; kernel: 5.1x over FlashAttention, 4.2x over FlashInfer, 10.6x over DeFT

limitations: Benefit depends on degree of KV prefix sharing (tree depth/breadth); greedy binary assignment may not always find the globally optimal grouping; limited evaluation on non-tree serving patterns.
